basis: Defining dysostosis multiplex with a lysosomal storage mechanism; an isolated thin corpus callosum finding does not establish common neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: LYSET deficiency disrupts lysosomal enzyme targeting, causing storage disease. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9547973/).

basis: Marrow disease, immunodeficiency and syndromic deafness define Emberger syndrome. Lymphedema is lymphatic; warts in 4/14 fall below 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: primary lymphatic malformation/lymphedema does not establish disease of the heart or blood vessels covered by this axis.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural deafness is a named defining component of the syndrome, despite variable expression.

basis: Acral dermatitis defines the concept; associated viral infections do not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism throughout this umbrella.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation and association with viral infection alone do not establish infection, autoimmunity or immune-mediated disease across the umbrella.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental, intestinal/salivary and hearing dysfunction; lacrimal failure in 2/2. Airway obstruction/mucus plugging and skeletal anomalies omitted at the four-organ cap.

decisions.pulmonary: none under cap: recurrent mucus plugging and choanal atresia qualify, but lacrimal failure in 2/2 has stronger frequency evidence than airway findings in 1/1.
decisions.ocular: involved: alacrima in 2/2 represents persistent loss of lacrimal function; retained as the fourth axis.

basis: Hyperinsulinism and deafness define syndrome; enteropathy/tubulopathy reported in ~3/18, absent in later 15. [Cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3579360/).

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: historical enteropathy occurred in 3 initial cases but 0/15 later cases (~17% overall); it is not a consistent defining criterion across the deletion syndrome.
decisions.otologic: primary: severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss is a consistent defining feature, including all 15 patients in the later cohort.

basis: Glycosylation defect with defining neurodevelopmental impairment (delay 11/11). Liver, enteropathy and coagulation findings are 5-29%; retinal degeneration 1-4%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurologic dysfunction explicitly defines ALG6-CDG; developmental delay occurs in 11/11, with ataxia and neurologic abnormalities at 30-79%.

basis: Microtia (5/5) and anorectal malformation (atresia 2/6) characterize syndrome; renal ectopia and vesicoureteral reflux each occur in 2/5 (~40%). Skeletal abnormalities lack common-frequency evidence.

decisions.renal: involved: renal ectopia and vesicoureteral reflux each occur in 2/5 (~40%); associated urinary malformations rather than the defining ear/anorectal phenotype.

basis: Immunodeficiency; eczema >50%, retained teeth needing extraction >50%, scoliosis >30%; lung disease is secondary. [Cohort](https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20191804).

decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic eczema affects >50% in the AD IL6ST cohort; direct immune dysregulation causes persistent dermatitis.

basis: Deafness, metacarpal/metatarsal synostosis and urethral hypospadias define syndrome; developmental/intellectual impairment in both reported cases (2/2).

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental/intellectual impairment in 2/2 reported cases; supplied PMID is incorrect. [Report](https://doi.org/10.1002/ajmg.a.30728).

basis: Biliary disease, developmental delay (4/6) and skeletal anomalies (polydactyly 4/7) define syndrome; renal insufficiency 2/6 (~33%). Pituitary/cardiac findings omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: involved: renal insufficiency in 2/6 (~33%) establishes direct common dysfunction; three primary slots retain more frequent defining manifestations.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal abnormalities are a named defining component, with polydactyly in 4/7 (~57%); prioritized among the three primary axes.
